title: mac-slot tests shared state with real slot runs: the caller's environment (MAC_SLOT_*, PATH with node_modules/.bin) reached the script under test, and afterEach SIGKILLed direct children only, then removed the folder, so grandchildren outlived their test and holder loops could run forever
evidence: tools/mac-slot.test.ts env() spread process.env and deleted only CI: with MAC_SLOT_MAX_LOAD=1 exported a run at load 1.00 refused with exit 75. afterEach killed tracked children only; a holder's forked shell naming the test folder survived it (both pinned failing first). Fd 9 inheritance checked and disproved 2026-11-13: under `sh tools/mac-slot.sh tests -- npx vitest run`, lsof showed fd 9 on ~/Library/Caches/health-roadmap-slots/tests.1 only in the `npm exec` process (or vitest itself when run directly); the vitest worker's fd 9 was another file and a spawned child had fds 0-2 only. Fixed in the test only (tools/mac-slot.sh unchanged): env() is built fresh (system PATH, HOME, TMPDIR); every child is spawned detached; afterEach TERMs then KILLs each tracked group, waits for it, then removes the folder; holder loops give up when their folder goes or after 120 s. Pins: a caller's MAC_SLOT_* and PATH change nothing and a decoy MAC_SLOT_HOME stays empty; a spawned child holds no fd 9 and nothing in the real slot folder; a test that fails mid-run leaves no process naming its folder (modelled on T22). US-71 AC11
